messages:
Priya Shah: Heads-up — last 3 nights we've had ~25 GPU memory-high pages during the kvcache eviction window (02:00-03:30). Paging the oncall every time is burning cycles. Thoughts on switching some of these to tickets when there's no user impact?
Alex Kim: +1, sounds noisy. Can we differentiate by impact? e.g. batch-job pools vs interactive/p90 latency.
Jamie Liu: We already have a basic SLO for request latency. Idea: keep pages for any alert that correlates with increased inference latency or failed requests, otherwise convert to ticket.
Chris Torres: Agree. Practically: use Prometheus to add a correlate check. If gpu_mem_high AND api_latency_p95 > 300ms then page, else ticket. Also group by node_pool to avoid fan-out.
Alex Kim: Draft PromQL for discussion:
```promql
(sum by(node_pool)(rate(gpu_memory_eviction_count[5m])) > 0) and
(sum by(node_pool)(histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, node_pool))) > 0.3)
```
(rough sketch)
Sofia Nguyen: Love the correlate approach. Two operational notes: 1) use a 10m for the non-impact cases before converting to a ticket so short blips don't surface; 2) add a mute window config for scheduled maintenance/kvcache flushes.
Priya Shah: +1 on 10m. For mute windows we should make them per-node-pool and time-bound (02:00-04:00). Need to be careful with training jobs that can actually saturate GPUs for hours.
Chris Torres: For grouping: set alertmanager group_by: [node_pool, job_type] and group_interval: 15m to batch duplicates. That will cut down multi-page storms when a single cluster flaps.
Jamie Liu: Also propose an experiment: for the next 2 weeks, convert pages -> tickets for node_pool=bulk-batch during 00:30-04:30 unless correlated with latency/failures. Track metrics: number of pages, ticket count, mean time to resolution, and any customer-visible errors.
Alex Kim: I'll open a PR with the alert rule changes plus a new Grafana panel 'sre/paging_vs_tickets' that shows pages by rule, tickets created, and correlated latency.
Priya Shah: Can we add a simple cost estimator? fewer pages -> fewer wakeups -> less overtime on-call and fewer preemptions on spot nodes. Rough calc: 20 pages/night * 30 nights * 30m avg wake time = 300 hours/month of oncall time.
Sofia Nguyen: I put together a minimal dashboard concept: panels: paging_count, tickets_created, correlated_latency_p95, paging_cost_estimate. Link: https://grafana.internal/r/abc123 (placeholder) :eyes:
ops-bot: experiment-toggle: "bulk-batch-night-mute" set to ON by Priya Shah at 2005002500
Chris Torres: Nice. Make sure we add a fallback page rule: if pages suppressed but node becomes NotReady or many pods crash, that still pages (node flapping is higher severity).
Priya Shah: Good catch. I'll include fallback rules in the RFC. Next steps: Alex to PR alert changes, Jamie to draft experiment runbook, Chris to update alertmanager grouping. We'll review tomorrow 10:30. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Alex Kim: On it — will push PR + link to runbook before EOD.
